clue.text: Second part of Bleak House it is in print

indicators.note: the second letter of the word Bleak is taken, signalled by 'Second part of'

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about the second instalment of Dickens's novel appearing in print.
explanation.walkthrough: Bleak House looks like the novel's title, but only Bleak is the source of a letter; House is abbreviated. 'is in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho is a lithograph, a print made by lithography.

clue.text: Old habits of Robert Louis's hero

definitions.meaning: old-fashioned long woollen underwear, a garment worn habitually
belonging to Long John Silver, the hero of Robert Louis Stevenson's Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A study of the old customs of Stevenson's swashbuckling hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' suggests customs but means clothing. Read the second definition as the possessive of Long John Silver's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Long underwear covering the legs is a garment, and habit is an old word for dress.

clue.text: Follow behind in great agony

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the letters of great agony

explanation.surface: Trailing along while suffering terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag on is to attach yourself to someone and follow behind them.

clue.text: Utter a slogan which was effective in 1997 election?

definitions.meaning: utter as an adjective means complete or total

definitions.text: a slogan which was effective in 1997 election?
definitions.meaning: in 1997 the Conservatives lost power, so '...!' reads as a winning slogan

explanation.surface: Speaking a political catchphrase that worked in the 1997 British general election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb, to say, but is the adjective. In 1997 Labour swept the Conservatives, the party of the right, out of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright and utter are synonyms meaning complete or absolute, as in an outright lie.

clue.text: Collection of cash for a creamy dessert and a sandwich?

parts.note: a whip is a dessert of whipped cream or egg whites
a round is a sandwich made from two whole slices of bread

explanation.surface: Asking everyone to chip in for pudding and a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: A round is British usage for a sandwich made of two full slices of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal collection of money among a group, for a gift or cause.

clue.text: Mark of prosperity, formerly

definitions.meaning: a raised mark on the skin, as from a lash
in archaic English the word meant wellbeing or prosperity, as in commonweal

explanation.surface: A sign of wealth in times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A weal is a welt raised on skin; in old usage the same word meant welfare.

clue.text: Believe me, Prometheus might have uttered this, anticipating his punishment

definitions.meaning: an emphatic phrase assuring the listener of something

definitions.text: Prometheus might have uttered this, anticipating his punishment
definitions.meaning: in myth Prometheus was chained to a rock as punishment, as in Prometheus Bound

explanation.surface: An assurance the Titan might have given, foreseeing his chains.
explanation.walkthrough: Prometheus stole fire for mankind and was chained to a rock by Zeus; Aeschylus's play is Prometheus Bound.
explanation.definitionFit: The old idiom 'I'll be bound' means I am sure, much like an emphatic believe me.

clue.text: Yak adopted as family pet?

definitions.meaning: to yak is to chatter, and British slang for chatter is to ... on
a common pet animal kept by families

explanation.surface: A Himalayan ox taken in as a household animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yak' looks like the animal but is the verb to chatter. 'adopted as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit means to talk on and on, as yakking does.

clue.text: A few inches, presumably, on the ground

definitions.meaning: a few inches is a length less than twelve inches, read as the phrase under a foot
lying about on the floor where people tread

explanation.surface: A small measurement taken at ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underfoot lies on the ground beneath one's feet, in the way.

clue.text: Daughter examined briefly, about to undergo treatment for addiction

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: ex. is a short form of examined
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is checked over quickly before entering rehab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as a phrase meaning on the point of, but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' is fodder; ex. is a standard short form of examined.
explanation.definitionFit: To detox is to undergo a course of withdrawal from drugs or alcohol.

clue.text: Old warrior with armour on read out well-known poem

indicators.note: read out signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a knight is a mediaeval warrior and mail is chain armour, so the phrase gives knight mail

explanation.surface: An ancient armoured fighter recites a famous verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight and night sound the same. Night Mail is W. H. Auden's poem written for a 1936 documentary about the London to Scotland mail train.
explanation.definitionFit: Night Mail is Auden's famous poem about the overnight postal train.

clue.text: Order extremely elegant bathroom accessory

parts.note: to bid is to command or order

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of elegant are taken

explanation.surface: Buying a very stylish fitting for the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like buying but means bid, to command; 'extremely' gives the first and last letters of elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low washing basin found in bathrooms.

clue.text: Drug addict has most of family hooked within a month

indicators.note: hooked within means caught inside, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: June is a month of the year

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word for family is dropped

parts.note: kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: An addict is said to have relatives hooked during a single month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooked within' reads as addiction in the surface, but it is the container signal; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A junkie is slang for a drug addict, especially one on heroin.

clue.text: She'll succeed, captivating one in her verbal deceptions

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word for deceptions is used by its sound

parts.note: tricks are deceptions
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A woman will prosper by charming someone with her clever lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal' tells you the deceptions are spelt as they sound; 'captivating' is the container signal and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heritrix is an heiress, a woman who will succeed to an inheritance.

clue.text: Individualist supplying endless drinks on the house

parts.note: on the house means given free of charge

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: spirits are strong alcoholic drinks

explanation.surface: A nonconformist providing unlimited drinks at the bar for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of SPIRITS; 'supplying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A free spirit is someone who lives independently, unconstrained by convention.

clue.text: Blow up, having, targeted building from the air?

definitions.meaning: to lose one's temper suddenly
a bomber that struck the top of a building literally struck its roof

explanation.surface: Exploding, having bombed a structure from above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' looks like an explosion but means to become very angry; the comma after 'having' is surface punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the roof is an idiom for becoming suddenly furious, like blowing up.

clue.text: German specialist flitting in and out during exam

indicators.note: during means inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a test is an exam

indicators.note: flitting means darting about, so the letters of in and out are rearranged

explanation.surface: An expert on Germany darts in and out of the examination hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two fodder words without giving letters; 'flitting' is the anagram signal and 'during' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Teutonist is a scholar or specialist in German language and culture.

clue.text: Common ailment caught by the elderly

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
old people are the elderly

explanation.surface: A frequent illness picked up by old people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like catching an illness but stands for C; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold is a mild viral infection, the commonest of ailments.

clue.text: A hundred centigrade is unusual in this holiday resort

indicators.note: is unusual signals the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for centigrade

explanation.surface: Temperatures of a hundred degrees are rare at this vacation spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unusual' rearranges A HUNDRED plus C; 'in this' is a link pointing to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude ranch is an American ranch run as a holiday resort for tourists.

clue.text: Put a bugging device in church if absolutely necessary

parts.note: a tap is a device for secretly listening to phone calls
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to plant a listening device in a church, but only if needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link; the clue's own word 'in' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch is an idiom meaning if really necessary, in an emergency.

clue.text: Blow creating draught

definitions.meaning: a hard punch or hit
a swig or gulp of a drink, especially spirits

explanation.surface: A gust of wind causing a draft through the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' and 'draught' suggest wind, but mean a punch and a gulp; 'creating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is both a heavy punch and a large swallow of liquor.

clue.text: Set forth after control is restored

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the first

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
to state is to set forth in words

explanation.surface: Once order is set out, it is brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstated means put back into a former position, that is restored.

clue.text: A series of downturns in the skiing business

definitions.text: A series of downturns in the skiing business

parts.words: A series of downturns in the skiing business
parts.note: downturns read as downhill turns made by a skier, not falls in trade

explanation.surface: Ski resorts suffer repeated commercial slumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a ski race down a zigzag course between gates, a series of turns.

clue.text: Writer dunking bread bun in drink

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, and a tope is a drink
a roll is a bread bun

explanation.surface: An author dips his bread roll into his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunking' is a link here; Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a prolific Victorian novelist, so a writer.

clue.text: Poet's big day coming up

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the poet

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a big clothing size
Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday, a day

explanation.surface: A poet's important day is approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns OS + SAT, giving the letters upwards. Torquato Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the Italian poet who wrote Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Reporter's observed a website designer?

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: spied means observed, so the phrase gives spied a

explanation.surface: A journalist has seen someone who builds internet pages.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the spoken words for 'spied a' match the answer. A web-site designer is a creature that spins a web.
explanation.definitionFit: This creature constructs webs, so whimsically it designs the site of a web.

clue.text: Tendency to stray

definitions.meaning: the general gist or tenor of something
to wander off course

explanation.surface: An inclination to wander.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift means the general tendency of an argument, and as a verb to wander aimlessly.

clue.text: Delay guy's visit

definitions.meaning: to ... is to postpone, as in a ... of execution
a rope or wire supporting a mast or tent, also called a guy
a period spent visiting somewhere

explanation.surface: Putting off a friend's trip to see someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man but is a supporting rope; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay means a postponement, a supporting rope, and a short sojourn.

clue.text: Refuse drink

definitions.meaning: kitchen waste fed to pigs
to gulp down greedily

explanation.surface: Turning down a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill is pig food made of scraps, and to swill is to guzzle drink.

clue.text: Internet surfing requires installation of zero memory

indicators.note: installation of means putting one piece inside another
surfing suggests moving about, so the letters of Internet are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Browsing the web needs memory that is set up from scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surfing' rearranges INTERNET to RETENTIN; 'installation of' puts O into it; 'requires' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the ability to keep things in mind, that is memory.

clue.text: Eye-care needed? Book test after work

indicators.note: after puts the book and test pieces following the work piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tome is a large book
to try is to test

explanation.surface: Does someone need an eye examination after reading a book?
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed?' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Optometry is the profession of testing eyesight and prescribing lenses.

clue.text: Using sophisticated technology out east creates a problem

indicators.note: out means the letter is removed

parts.note: hi-tech describes advanced technology

explanation.surface: Advanced technology from the Orient causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out east' looks like the Orient but removes E from HITECH; 'creates a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or temporary problem.
